clue.text: Nominal subscription

parts.note: a subscription in the old sense is a name written at the foot of a document, and it is nominal because it consists of one's own name

explanation.definitionFit: Subscribing a letter means writing your name beneath it, the mark that authenticates the document.

clue.text: Be sparing with cream on top of pie

parts.note: to cream milk is to skim it, taking off the top layer

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means the first letter of the word pie

explanation.surface: A cook is told not to overdo the cream topping on a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' looks like a noun; it is the verb to skim.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise, giving too little, is to be stingy with something.

clue.text: Bitterness over English appearing on Spanish ship

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above, before, the next

parts.note: gall means bitterness or rancour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Resentment at an English presence on a ship from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places GALL above E; 'appearing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sailing warship of the 16th century, typical of the Armada.

clue.text: Port — a variety passed round right to left

indicators.note: passed round means the letters for right and left are put around the word for variety

parts.note: variety means change, as in a change being as good as a rest

explanation.surface: A bottle of port of some vintage is passed round the table from right to left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine passed at dinner; it is a harbour city in northern Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkhangelsk, on the White Sea, is a Russian seaport, traditionally spelt this way in English.

clue.text: Blue material 14ac mixed

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred together in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 14 across is a vessel, URN

explanation.surface: Blue fabric blended with something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' is anagram fodder, not fabric; 'mixed' rearranges it with URN from 14 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, bright shade made from lapis lazuli, a kind of rich blue pigment.

clue.text: Mischievous child finishing the plateful off

indicators.note: finishing points to the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster clears the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing' looks like eating up; it picks the last letters of THE, PLATEFUL, OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A small impish youngster can be called a little sprite or imp.

clue.text: Sort of crossword one's said to always remember

explanation.surface: A puzzle type that, so the saying goes, nobody ever forgets.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo was a celebrated elephant at London Zoo, and elephants are said never to forget.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant puzzle is billed as a jumbo crossword, and an elephant (Jumbo being the famous zoo elephant) proverbially never forgets.

clue.text: Early factory machine producing disastrous pocketing

explanation.surface: An old mill machine causing a costly mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a billiards term for an in-off, sending one's own ball into a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Hargreaves's spinning machine was an early textile mill invention; in billiards the term names a shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket, losing points.

clue.text: Among limes, quite small tree of another sort

indicators.note: among says the answer sits inside the run of letters in the following words

explanation.surface: Among lime trees there stands a quite different small tree.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a variant spelling of mesquite; 'of another sort' contrasts it with the limes.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny shrub or small tree of the American southwest, a kind of leguminous plant.

clue.text: Defeat as result of poor fielding

explanation.surface: A loss caused by bad fielding.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an overthrow is a fielder's return that misses the stumps, letting the batsmen run more.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple a ruler is to defeat him, and in cricket a wild throw past the stumps gives away extra runs.

clue.text: Sick Parisian here? Therapy's beginning for invalid

parts.note: sick means ill
ici is French for here, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here taken from 'Therapy's'

explanation.surface: An ailing Frenchman in hospital asks how his treatment is starting for an invalid patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' looks like a noun for a sick person; read it as in-valid, not lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful or forbidden is not valid in law.

clue.text: German city provided backing for manoeuvre at bridge

indicators.note: backing tells us the city and the condition are read together from end to start

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr
provided means if, as a condition

explanation.surface: A card manoeuvre funded by a German city sounds like sponsorship of a bridge tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the city and the condition round as one run. 'manoeuvre at bridge' is the card game, not a river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a finesse is a technical play trying to win a trick with a lower card while a higher one is out.

clue.text: Greek letters in work of art

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
eta is another letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Inscriptions in Greek appear on a painting or sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, Michelangelo's being the most famous.

clue.text: Young man, losing head, at random may turn to her

definitions.text: Young man, losing head, at random may turn to her

indicators.note: random signals that the letters before it are thrown together in a new order
losing its head means the word man drops its first letter

explanation.surface: A youth who has lost his composure may seek the advice of a newspaper columnist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts MAN to AN; YOUNG plus AN plus AT, rearranged under 'random', give the answer. The whole clue also describes who might write to her.
explanation.definitionFit: An advice columnist answers readers' personal problems, the kind a troubled youth might send in.

clue.text: Way in which they were knocked in the air

definitions.text: Way in which they were knocked in the air

parts.words: Way in which they were knocked in the air
parts.note: a music-hall song says they knocked 'em in a certain London street; 'in the air' means in a tune, not tossed upward

explanation.walkthrough: Albert Chevalier's song chorus runs 'Wot cher! Knocked 'em in the' street; the street is also the cheapest square on the London Monopoly board.
explanation.definitionFit: The street of the old cockney song 'Wot Cher!' is a road, a way, in south-east London.

clue.text: Vessel to make sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for 'make' is spoken and the spelling heard is what goes in

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting a container to ring out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a verb meaning to resonate; it is the homophone signal on EARN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vase-like container, as for ashes or tea, is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Not getting a reference, say, so denied clear prospects

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken and the spelling with the same sound is entered

parts.note: not referred to or quoted is uncited

explanation.surface: A job applicant lacking a reference finds career prospects closed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reference' looks like a job reference; it is a citation.
explanation.definitionFit: A player whose view is blocked cannot see clearly.

clue.text: Chips, for example, hard to beat on board

explanation.surface: A man nicknamed Chips proves unbeatable at a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Chips is the beloved elderly teacher in James Hilton's novel 'Goodbye, Mr Chips'; the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Chips of the novel is a revered old schoolmaster, a grand old teacher; chess players of the highest rank hold the title and are hard to beat.

clue.text: A new Italian city's becoming state capital

parts.note: Napoli is the Italian name for Naples, and the 's adds its S

explanation.surface: A new Italian city rises to become a regional capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's here supplies a letter; 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Maryland, a US state, home of the Naval Academy.

clue.text: Decoy manoeuvre pilot goes on

indicators.note: manoeuvre asks for the letters of the following words to be moved into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An aircraft pilot keeps flying a decoy manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' looks like part of a flying phrase but signals rearranging PILOT GOES ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A police informer or a bird used to lure others is a decoy.

clue.text: Getting old in the ring, and less menacing

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: in puts the letter for old inside the word for less

parts.note: less means minus, as in subtraction

explanation.surface: An ageing boxer in the ring becomes less threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ring' looks like a boxing ring; it is the letter O. 'Getting' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Threatening or foreboding, as of dark clouds.

clue.text: Headquarters in Cornwall and West Devon, perhaps

indicators.note: head quarter means the first quarter of the word Cornwall, two of its eight letters

explanation.surface: An organisation's head office located in Cornwall and western Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headquarters' splits into head quarter: the first quarter of CORNWALL is CO. 'Devon' wants to be a county; it is a breed of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Devon is a breed of red beef cattle, and a female of it is an example of the farm animal.

clue.text: Fanciful conception in correspondence with artist

parts.note: to chime with something is to correspond or agree with it
RA is a Royal Academician, a standard artist

explanation.surface: A whimsical idea arises in letters exchanged with a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' looks like letters; it means agreement. 'in' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild illusory notion, after the fire-breathing monster of myth.

clue.text: Following young man's advice, and so perishing

explanation.surface: Taking the old advice given to a youth, and dying as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: The advice 'Go west, young man' is attributed to Horace Greeley; going west also means dying or being lost.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Go west, young man' was the famous call to settle the American frontier, and to go that way is slang for to die.

clue.text: Stern and bow of yacht in need of cleaning

parts.note: stern means grim

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a boat, so the first letter of yacht

explanation.surface: Back and front of a yacht need a scrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' and 'bow' look nautical; stern is grim, bow is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in ingrained dirt.

clue.text: Labour in trouble

explanation.definitionFit: Efforts taken over a task are its labour, and to take care or bother over something is to take trouble.

clue.text: Only daughter did some work at last

parts.note: sole means only, as a sole survivor

explanation.surface: An only daughter finally got something done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' looks like finally; a last is a cobbler's foot-shaped block on which shoes are made.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler fitting new undersides to shoes works on a last.

clue.text: First prime — the age to be unfaithful?

parts.note: two is the smallest prime number
an age or era is a time

explanation.surface: A maths question about the earliest prime number turns into a question of fidelity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First prime' suggests the best or the number one; it is the smallest prime number.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive a partner by seeing someone else in secret is to cheat on them.

clue.text: Reveals oddly gutted fish

indicators.note: oddly gutted means the odd-numbered letters are removed, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A gutted fish lays bare its insides oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing letters 1, 3, 5, 7 of REVEALS leaves E, E, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A long snakelike fish.

clue.text: Minimize friction that's result of strike, perhaps

explanation.surface: Reduce friction, the way a successful strike does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like industrial action; it is finding oil when drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: To lubricate thoroughly reduces friction, and a successful drilling strike yields a gushing petroleum source.

clue.text: Attractive girl has brief fling

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana
a shy is a quick throw, a short fling as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A good-looking woman enjoys a short romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' looks like a romance; it is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for good-looking, sexy.

clue.text: Dismal day suffered as servant

indicators.note: suffered says the letters of the words before it have been knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A gloomy day endured by a domestic worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A female attendant who looks after a lady's clothes and hair is a domestic servant.
